bracket.title: How the bracket works
bracket.text: The 2026-27 College Football Playoff takes 12 teams. The ACC, Big Ten, Big 12, and SEC champions are automatic. Until those games are played, this projection uses the highest-ranked team in each of those conferences. One more automatic bid goes to the highest-ranked team from the American, Conference USA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac-12, or Sun Belt, whether or not it won its conference. Notre Dame is automatic if it is in the top 12, and the field then takes six at-large teams. Otherwise it takes seven. Automatic qualifiers ranked outside the top 12 are seeded at the bottom, in rank order. The four highest-ranked teams in the field are seeds 1–4 and get a first-round bye. They do not have to be conference champions. The first round is on the higher seed's campus: 5 vs. 12, 6 vs. 11, 7 vs. 10, and 8 vs. 9. Quarterfinals are not reseeded. The winner of 8/9 plays 1, the winner of 5/12 plays 4, the winner of 7/10 plays 2, and the winner of 6/11 plays 3. Seeds 1–3 pick the quarterfinal sites, and the semifinal that follows a win, on Selection Day, Dec. 6, 2026. This page does not assign those bowls.

selection.title: How bowl selection works
selection.text: A team needs six wins to be bowl-eligible. The College Football Playoff field is filled first. Conferences then fill the remaining games through their tie-ins and selection order, and open spots can be filled at large. If bowls still need teams after the six-win pool is used, a 5-7 team can fill a spot. Those 5-7 teams had been taken in order of the multiyear Academic Progress Rate. In May 2026 the NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision Oversight Committee voted to adopt a proposal that lets the conference choose a 5-7 team with a multiyear APR of at least 930 instead. ESPN reported the same committee vote.

money.title: Payouts and the CFP pool
money.text: Bowl and CFP money is paid to conferences, not directly to the teams. For 2026-27, CFP revenue shares other than expenses are not finalized. Each conference whose team plays in the CFP receives a $3.18 million expense stipend per round. The 2025-26 schedule, labeled that way on the CFP cards, was $300,000 per school that met the APR standard, $4 million for each CFP team and another $4 million for each team that reached a quarterfinal, $6 million for each team that reached a semifinal and another $6 million for each team in the championship game, and a $3 million expense stipend per conference per round.
